name: Business casual

card.summary: A workplace dress code between suits and everyday casual wear, with chinos or slacks, collared shirts and loafers, which people use to look polished and put-together without a full suit.
card.note: Definitions vary by employer and country, so the exact items differ from workplace to workplace.

quick.overview:
Business casual is a dress code that sits between a formal business suit and everyday casual clothes. For men it usually means dress shirt and trousers or chinos without a matching suit jacket, with a tie optional; for women, a blouse or shirt with trousers, a skirt or a dress.

The appearance payoff is a neat, put-together look that reads as professional. Studies of clothing and perception, mostly in healthcare and workplace settings, find that attire style shapes how trustworthy or ethical a person is judged to be.
quick.how: People build a business casual wardrobe from tailored chinos or slacks, oxford or button-down shirts, polos or sweaters, an optional unstructured blazer and leather shoes such as loafers. Guides stress clean, pressed, well-fitting clothes in neutral colors such as navy, gray and black.
quick.risks: No health risks. The practical issue is ambiguity: there is no universal definition, and what counts as acceptable changes between employers, industries and countries.

lead: Business casual is a form of smart casual dress for white-collar workplaces, replacing the traditional business suit. Wikipedia notes there is no generally agreed definition and that sources vary [1].

For men it usually means the components of a suit without the matching jacket, typically a dress shirt and trousers, with a tie optional and a blazer, sweater or vest as choices; for women the same pieces in a feminine style, or a dress or skirt at or just above the knee [1]. It is used to look polished and approachable. Studies of attire and perception, including surveys of patients and workers, report that clothing style affects judgments of professionalism and ethicality [2][3].

angle.text: Clothing is a visible part of appearance, and business casual is a way to choose fit, color and formality. Guides describe pressed, well-fitting separations in navy, gray and black as the core of the look.

paras: University career centers cited by Wikipedia give varied definitions: Marquette University includes khakis, slacks and skirts plus polos and long-sleeved shirts and excludes T-shirts and sweatshirts; Virginia Tech recommends darker neutral colors, with clothing pressed and crisp; and the University of Toronto describes a classic, clean-cut look where a full suit is not required [1].

A 2011 Financial Times column described the men's version as chinos, a blazer and a good shirt with no tie, and a 2011 BBC article named a button-down shirt, jacket or blazer, khaki or gray slacks and leather shoes a safe global standard while noting that norms vary by country [1].

Wikipedia traces US acceptance to Casual Fridays in California, themselves inspired by Hawaii's Aloha Friday custom of the 1960s [1]. Grokipedia dates early adoption to Silicon Valley technology firms in the early 1980s, a 1991 policy at Alcoa, and the 1995 relaxation of IBM's dress code under Lou Gerstner, and cites survey figures showing casual-dress policies spreading to a majority of US companies through the 1990s [4]. After 2020, remote and hybrid work were reported to shift norms further toward relaxed smart-casual items [4].

A study in the Journal of Business Ethics, using two laboratory studies with working samples, found casual attire was perceived as less ethical than business casual attire [2]. A randomized pharmacy study of 179 university staff varied pharmacist dress between casual, business casual and formal, with and without a white coat, and measured satisfaction, trust and service quality [5].

In a pediatric ophthalmology clinic survey of 149 families, most respondents preferred a white coat, and men preferred professional attire to business casual [6]. A 2019 survey of 505 adults rated photos of physicians in business casual or professional attire, with and without a white coat [7].

No studies found on business casual as an intervention. The attire-perception studies above are surveys and laboratory experiments in healthcare and workplace settings rather than clinical trials [2][5][6][7].

timeline.event: Hawaii's Aloha Friday custom, later credited as an inspiration for Casual Fridays [1].
Silicon Valley technology firms encourage relaxed dress [4].
Alcoa adopts a business casual policy at its Pittsburgh headquarters [4].
IBM relaxes its dress code under Lou Gerstner [4].
